text:
lina: Hi team 44b. First day at Redwood! I'm on openSUSE Leap 15.4 and trying to bootstrap the repo. Running into two things: `asdf install` for node/python fails complaining about missing `pkg-config`/`readline`, and the repo `./bootstrap.sh` aborts because it can't find direnv and my `.envrc` (I don't yet have 1Password access). Any SUSE folks who can point me to the right packages?

pablo: welcome Lina! openSUSE package names are a bit different. Try:

```
sudo zypper refresh
sudo zypper install -t pattern devel_basis pkg-config libopenssl-devel libreadline-devel ncurses-devel libbz2-devel libffi-devel xz
```

Those usually cover asdf builds for both python and node. After that, restart your shell and try `asdf install` again.

lina: thanks Pablo 44d. I tried the pattern but `asdf install nodejs 18.16.0` still fails with gyp/OpenSSL link errors. I installed `libopenssl-devel` but the build system still can't find the headers.

ev an: on SUSE sometimes pkg-config paths are not picked up by the build; try exporting the paths explicitly. Example:

```
export LDFLAGS="-L/usr/lib64"
export CPPFLAGS="-I/usr/include"
export PKG_CONFIG_PATH="/usr/lib64/pkgconfig:/usr/share/pkgconfig"
```

Then `asdf install nodejs 18.16.0`. If you're using a local Homebrew (linuxbrew) you'll want to prefer brew's openssl and set flags to the brew prefix instead.

lina: that fixed node, thanks. For python build I still saw `readline` not found even though I installed `libreadline-devel`. Any ideas?

pablo: make sure `ncurses-devel` is installed and that your shell session is fresh. Also `python` build looks for `libncurses` on SUSE under `ncurses-devel`. You can also check `rpm -ql ncurses-devel` to find include paths. If you used brew previously, check there's no conflicting headers in the environment.

lina: ok python worked after installing `ncurses-devel` and restarting the terminal. Next: `./bootstrap.sh` expects `direnv` and `.envrc` and tries to `ssh-add` an `~/.ssh/id_ed25519`. I haven't generated keys yet and infra hasn't given me 1Password access. What's the recommended temporary flow?

rachel: welcome! We prefer new hires to generate their own SSH keypair: `ssh-keygen -t ed25519 -C "lina@redwood"`. Add the public key to your GitHub/Redwood account once you have access. For the `.envrc`, copy `env.example` to `.env.local` and create a minimal `.envrc` like `source .env.local` or `export $(cat .env.local | xargs)` then `direnv allow`. Use placeholder values for secrets until infra provisions 1Password.

lina: I can do that. One last snag: I tried to import my GPG key for commit signing and VS Code can't find the agent socket. I'm running GNOME on SUSE.

ev an: on GNOME, ensure `gnupg2` is installed and the gpg-agent is running. Add to your shell rc:

```
export GPG_TTY=$(tty)
export SSH_AUTH_SOCK=$(gpgconf --list-dirs agent-ssh-socket)
```

Then `gpgconf --launch gpg-agent`. For VS Code, enable SSH/GPG agent forwarding in Remote settings if using remote sessions. If the key is in the system keyring, sometimes you need `pinentry-gnome3` so passphrase prompts show up.

lina: thanks, that made the key visible to VS Code. infra-bot: any ETA on 1Password access?

infra-bot: [onboarding] Ticket ONB-3412 created for Lina. Infra will provision 1Password and repo access today.

lina: great 64f. One housekeeping question: the repo has `server/.tool-versions` but not at the root and `./bootstrap.sh` expects a root `.tool-versions`. Should I copy it or is there a better pattern?

pablo: copy `server/.tool-versions` to repo root for local dev (`cp server/.tool-versions .`) or run `ASDF_ENV_FILE=server/.tool-versions ./bootstrap.sh` if you prefer not to copy. We usually copy when onboarding since it's simpler.

lina: final: what quickchecks should I run before pinging eng for CI runs?

ev an: run `make ci-local`, `scripts/check-env`, and `make lint` (fast). If those pass, open a draft PR and ping your onboarding buddy.

lina: perfect 44b. I'll add these openSUSE-specific notes to my onboarding doc. Thanks for the quick help everyone!

rachel: welcome aboard Lina! Ping me if you want a short pairing to walk the service and local dev flow.
